---
title: linearity of expectation
tags: [mathematics]
---

## Prompt

State and prove linearity for two real random variables. Is independence required?

## Statement

If $X,Y$ are integrable real random variables on the same probability space and $a,b\in\mathbb R$, then

$$
\mathbb E[aX+bY]=a\mathbb E[X]+b\mathbb E[Y].
$$

Independence is not required.

## Proof

The triangle inequality gives $|aX+bY|\leq |a||X|+|b||Y|$, so $aX+bY$ is integrable.
Linearity of the integral then gives

$$
\int_\Omega(aX+bY)\,dP=a\int_\Omega X\,dP+b\int_\Omega Y\,dP.
$$

Both variables are integrated against the same joint probability measure; no factorisation or independence assumption appears.
